That completes it. Pressing Search on the quoted phrase kept only "Law and Order in the Early City" — the one where those three words sit together in that order — and correctly dropped the one that just had the same words scattered around, the one with them reversed, and the note that happened to mention law and order separately. And it spelled out that the "and" in the middle was being treated as plain text, not a command. That's precisely the escape hatch I wanted.

Keeping it case-insensitive at the same time is right too — I don't want to have to match capitals to find my own phrase.

So that rounds out search for me: broad and forgiving by default, able to single out tags, combine with and/or/not and grouping, and a way to lock an exact phrase when I need it. Happy with search. What's next?
